summary: Feed s175_triple is degraded for IDS: 25.5% of TCP sessions are one-way, 6.8% of TCP packets show sequence gaps indicating drops, and 11.0% of frames are sliced to 256 bytes. IDS requires both directions and full payload for stream reassembly and signature matching, so detection coverage is significantly reduced.

findings.root_cause: Only one direction of TCP conversations is reaching the tool (37/145 sessions = 25.5% one-way, threshold 10%). Most likely the packet broker is forwarding only RX or TX from a single tap/SPAN leg without aggregating both directions, or asymmetric routing is captured at a single point. IDS needs both directions is true.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS cannot reassemble TCP streams, track state, or correlate request/response. Results in missed detections, broken flow records, and high false-negative rate for bidirectional signatures.

params.ensure_both_legs: combine RX+TX from paired tap/SPAN sources at broker

recommended_fix.why: Aggregate both directions of each flow to the same IDS tool port so stateful inspection sees complete sessions.

findings.root_cause: 124/1836 TCP packets (6.8%, threshold 1%) show sequence gaps by IP length analysis. Feed is noted as sliced yet drops persist, indicating packet broker egress congestion/buffer drops or SPAN oversubscription before the 1 Gbps IDS port. Tool overload check is healthy, so loss is upstream of tool.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS misses packets mid-stream causing failed reassembly, missed signatures, and evasion opportunity. 6.8% loss is well above IDS tolerance and degrades detection coverage.

recommended_fix.why: Reduce per-port load and buffer pressure by load-balancing or filtering to eliminate broker drops and ensure lossless delivery to 1G IDS.

findings.root_cause: 213/1930 frames (11.0%, threshold 5%) are cut short, most to 256 bytes snaplen. Packet broker is configured to slice packets to save bandwidth. IDS needs_full_payload is true and max_frame_bytes is 1518, so slicing removes L7 payload.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS cannot inspect full payload for signatures, malware, or exploit detection. Truncated frames cause signature mismatches and blind spots for any detection beyond headers.

recommended_fix.why: IDS requires full payload; disable broker slicing/snaplen and forward full 1518B frames to restore payload visibility.
